title: The Missing Cipher
premise: True-crime podcaster Wren Marchetti has built her reputation quietly closing cold cases the police mislabeled, but nothing prepares her for the Hollowbrook disappearance of 1995: a young archivist named Ivy Solano who vanished without a trace. When Ivy's diary surfaces at an estate sale, its entries continue for three weeks past the date she 'disappeared'—written in a cipher only Wren, with her late mother's linguistics notes, can begin to crack. Following the coded trail into Hollowbrook's founding families, Wren discovers Ivy was close to exposing a land-and-money conspiracy that still runs the town, and that the diary's final entries were written by someone else entirely—someone keeping Ivy alive, hidden, or worse. As Wren closes in, she must choose between publishing the truth and protecting the one person who can testify: Ivy herself, now living under a new name, whose silence has been the price of her survival. In the end, Wren exposes the conspiracy at the cost of her podcast's corporate backing, gains a found family in Ivy and the allies who helped her, and learns that some love—like some truth—is worth every duty it breaks.
about_author: Mirabel Kavanagh is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unsolved case files before turning to fiction, and her novels are known for their forensic attention to detail and quiet, aching emotional undercurrents. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast, where she claims every story begins with a document that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: The Estate Sale
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Between episodes of her podcast, Wren browses a rural estate sale and buys a box of papers containing Ivy Solano's diary—dated 1995, the year of Hollowbrook's most famous disappearance. Flipping through, she finds entries continuing three weeks beyond the official date Ivy vanished. The beat: the electric chill of a case that doesn't add up.

chapters.title: Three for Three
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, with a flashback to her first solved case. We learn how Wren quietly cracked three 'accidental' deaths, earning her a loyal but small audience and the wariness of Detective Amara Osei, who once arrested her for obstruction. The diary feels like case number four—except no one died, officially. The beat: ambition shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV in Hollowbrook. She interviews aging residents who repeat the official story: Ivy Solano, 24, ran away after a failed romance. But the town librarian, Ruth Ellery, hesitates too long before agreeing, and slips Wren a photocopied page of town council minutes from 1995. The beat: the first hairline crack in thirty years of silence.

chapters.title: Cipher
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, late nights in her apartment. The diary's final entries dissolve into a substitution cipher keyed to something Wren can't identify—until she recognizes her late mother's linguistic notation system in the margins, meaning Ivy and her mother crossed paths. The beat: grief and obsession braided together as the case becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The decoded fragments name four families who still dominate Hollowbrook: the Vances, the Merricks, the Okonkwos, and the Ashfords. In 1995 they pushed through a land consolidation deal that erased a historic Black neighborhood—and Ivy, an archivist, was cataloguing what was demolished. The beat: the machinery of power coming into focus.

chapters.title: Amara
chapters.summary: Detective Amara Osei's POV. Now Hollowbrook's police chief, Amara reads Wren's public records requests and knows exactly what she's chasing—she looked at the Solano file as a young officer and was told to close it. She drives to warn Wren off, but leaves more unsettled than she arrived. The beat: duty at war with conscience.

chapters.title: The Man in the Archive
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the county records office, someone has been pulling the same 1995 files ahead of her—a silver-haired man who introduces himself as Theodore Vance, the deal's surviving architect, all charm and menace. He offers Wren funding for her podcast. She declines. That night, her apartment is searched. The beat: the hunt reverses.

chapters.title: Alibi, Thirty Years Old
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reconstructs the night Ivy vanished: every founding family member has an airtight alibi—too airtight, rehearsed, corroborated by the same two witnesses. She maps the overlaps and finds a gap: the alibis only work if Ivy left town by 8 p.m. The diary says otherwise. The beat: the elegant, terrible shape of a coordinated lie.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession
chapters.summary: Ruth Ellery's POV. The librarian remembers Ivy vividly—they were close, more than friends, in a town that would never have allowed it. Ruth admits she destroyed a letter Ivy sent her in 1995 because Vance's people threatened the library's funding. What she kept: the envelope, postmarked not from Hollowbrook but from a coastal town two hundred miles away. The beat: love that survived by burying itself.

chapters.title: The Listener
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A listener email arrives with no text, only a photograph of Wren's own car outside Ruth's library. Someone inside the conspiracy is watching her—and, oddly, someone else seems to be watching them. Wren realizes the conspiracy isn't monolithic; someone is feeding her breadcrumbs. The beat: paranoia sharpened by an unexpected ally.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Notes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, with flashbacks to her mother. Wren finally decodes the cipher fully using her mother's notation system and learns the truth: Ivy didn't run. She was nearly killed at the consolidation site, saved by a guilt-wracked insider—Merrick's son Daniel—who hid her, faked her disappearance, and dictated the final diary entries himself so the town would stop searching. The beat: the coldest case cracks open.

chapters.title: What Happened to Daniel
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara pulls Daniel Merrick's file: he died in 1998, officially a boating accident—the fourth 'accident' in Hollowbrook in three years, and the one that made young Amara start her own quiet file. She realizes Wren's three solved cases were all cleanup kills. She calls Wren for the first time in years. The beat: two loners choosing each other's side.

chapters.title: The Middle of It
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the postmark and Daniel's hidden-money trail, Wren reaches the coastal town—and finds Ivy Solano alive, sixty-ish, going by another name, tending a garden. Ivy's first words: 'You shouldn't have come. They check on me every year.' The beat: the impossible made flesh, immediately shadowed by danger.

chapters.title: Ivy
chapters.summary: Ivy Solano's POV, her first chapter. Ivy tells her story: the archive, the threat, the attack, Daniel's rescue, and the bargain—her silence for her life, enforced by an annual 'wellness visit' from Vance's fixer. She stayed hidden because Daniel died proving what happens when she doesn't. The beat: thirty years of survival, and the exhaustion underneath it.

chapters.title: The Annual Visit
chapters.summary: Wren and Ivy's alternating POV. The fixer, Cole Ashford—youngest of the founding generation, the one who's kept the bargain for three decades—arrives early and finds Wren's rental car. Instead of raising the alarm, he warns them: Theodore Vance is dying and wants the secret buried permanently before he goes; Cole no longer wants to be the keeper of it. The beat: the enemy's own conscience fractures the wall.

chapters.title: Evidence of a Life
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ivy's evidence is thin after thirty years—the archive copies burned, Daniel's letters lost in the 'accident.' But Ivy remembers where the original land records were hidden: sealed in the Hollowbrook library's foundation stone during the 1995 renovation, placed there by Ruth. The beat: fragile hope, and the growing bond between Wren and Ivy.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, Wren's POV. Ruth, Amara, and Cole converge on the coastal town—an archivist, a cop, and a fixer who should be enemies, cooking dinner in Ivy's kitchen while Wren drafts the plan. Ivy, who has spent thirty years being no one, is suddenly surrounded by people who chose her. The beat: the warmth of a family assembled, not inherited.

chapters.title: Vance Moves
chapters.summary: Theodore Vance's POV. Dying and ruthless, Vance learns Cole has turned. He activates the last lever: he has proof that Amara's own father, a 1995 councilman, signed the demolition order—and he offers Amara her father's redemption in exchange for delivering Ivy. The beat: power corrupting even the offer of grace.

chapters.title: The Price of Duty
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara meets Vance and lets him believe she's taken the deal—while wearing a wire and carrying the recovered foundation-stone records, authenticated by Ruth and Wren. The meeting nearly collapses when Vance's lawyer spots the recorder; Amara stalls with the truth about her father, buying the minutes she needs. The beat: love against duty, resolved by refusing the choice.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, climax part one. Vance's men corner Wren and Ivy at the coastal house to destroy the diary and its living witness. Cole intervenes, taking a beating that lands him in the hospital, while Amara's team—tipped by the wire—arrives to arrest the fixers. Vance himself, watching from his car, is served a federal warrant as his oxygen tank runs low. The beat: terror breaking into deliverance.

chapters.title: Ivy Solano, Present Tense
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV, climax part two. In the Hollowbrook courthouse, Ivy testifies—her voice steady, her real name spoken aloud for the first time in thirty years. The town that erased a neighborhood and a woman must hear both named. Vance dies before sentencing; the surviving conspirators face charges; the demolished neighborhood's descendants file to reclaim the land. The beat: grief and vindication in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Missing Cipher
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, epilogue. Wren publishes the final episode—narrated with Ivy sitting beside her—then shuts down the corporate podcast and starts an independent one with Amara as her legal consultant and Ruth as her archivist. The last scene: the four of them, plus a recovering Cole, planting a garden at the rebuilt archive. The cipher is solved; the family is found. The beat: quiet, earned peace.
